In [[general topology]], a '''remote point''' is a [[Point (geometry)|point]] <math>p</math> that belongs to the [[Stone–Čech compactification]] <math>\beta X</math> of a [[Tychonoff space]] <math>X</math> but that does not belong to the [[topological closure]] within <math>\beta X</math> of any [[nowhere dense]] subset of <math>X</math>.<ref name="Van Douwen1978">{{cite journal|last1=Van Douwen|first1=Eric K.|authorlink=Eric van Douwen|title=Existence and applications of remote points|journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=84|issue=1|year=1978|pages=161–164|issn=0002-9904|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1978-14454-1|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Let <math>\R</math> be the [[real line]] with the standard topology. In 1962, [[Nathan Fine]] and [[Leonard Gillman]] proved that, assuming the [[continuum hypothesis]]:
{{blockquote|There exists a point <math>p</math> in <math>\beta \R</math> that is not in the closure of ''any'' [[discrete subset]] of <math>\R</math> ...<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-1962-0143172-5|title=Remote points in <math>\beta R</math>|year=1962|last1=Fine|first1=Nathan J.|last2=Gillman|first2=Leonard|journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=13|pages=29–36|doi-access=free}}</ref>}}

Their proof works for any Tychonoff space that is [[separable space|separable]] and not [[pseudocompact]].<ref name="Van Douwen1978"/>

Chae and [[Jeffrey H. Smith|Smith]] proved that the existence of remote points is independent, in terms of [[Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory]], of the continuum hypothesis for a class of topological spaces that includes [[metric spaces]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/0166-8641(80)90023-1|title=Remote points and G-spaces|year=1980|last1=Chae|first1=Soo Bong|last2=Smith|first2=Jeffrey H.|journal=[[Topology and Its Applications]]|volume=11|issue=3|pages=243–246|doi-access=}}</ref> Several other mathematical theorems have been proved concerning remote points.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://msp.org/pjm/1983/105-1/p06.xhtml|title=Spaces without remote points|journal=[[Pacific Journal of Mathematics]]|date=March 1983|volume=105|issue=1|pages=69–75|last1=Van Mill|first1=Jan|last2=Van Douwen|first2=Eric|doi=10.2140/pjm.1983.105.69|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="Dow1983">{{cite journal|last1=Dow|first1=Alan|title=Remote points in large products|journal=Topology and Its Applications|volume=16|issue=1|year=1983|pages=11–17|issn=0166-8641|doi=10.1016/0166-8641(83)90003-2|doi-access=}}</ref>
